decision: Primary target is Sales; Customers is a secondary target with its own model.
reason: Dashboard needs both outputs; Customers is not in test.csv, so it cannot feed the sales model.

decision: Main forecast horizon is 42 days; the same pipeline covers the 48-day test window.
reason: Brief asks for six weeks ahead; test.csv spans 48 days.

decision: Final holdout = last 42 labelled days of train, scored once after all choices are locked.
reason: Gives an honest estimate of forecast error; test.csv has no Sales to score against.

decision: Three earlier rolling 42-day validation windows with common cut-offs across stores.
reason: Tests stability across time without touching the final holdout.

decision: Model log1p(Sales); loss = RMSE on the log scale; primary metric = RMSPE on positive-sales days; MAE and RMSE secondary.
reason: Sales is right-skewed and finance cares about percentage error; log RMSE behaves like relative error.

decision: Predict zero when a store is closed; train on open days only.
reason: All closed days have zero sales; including them would distort the model.

decision: Do not cap Sales with IQR rules; treat outliers only with evidence from store histories.
reason: High sales may be genuine holiday or promotion peaks the model must learn.

decision: No actual future Customers or Sales may be used as forecast inputs; history is allowed only before the forecast origin.
reason: Prevents leakage; Customers is not available in test.csv.

decision: Use a shared LSTM across stores (store and calendar inputs) as the main deep learning design.
reason: More practical than 1,115 separate models and runs in Colab.

decision: Build the app with Streamlit and host it on a free platform.
reason: Brief allows Streamlit; free hosting is sufficient for the project.

decision: Unit tests, CI/CD and Docker are optional; list as pending if skipped.
reason: Not required by the brief; avoid claiming work that was not done.

decision: Settings (paths, seed 42, horizon, tracking names) live in src/config.py; one logger and one style module are shared by notebook and app.
reason: A single source of truth keeps results, figures and the app consistent.

decision: MLflow uses a local SQLite store (mlflow.db); models are logged as pickles (cloudpickle); trial run kept in a separate 'setup-check' experiment.
reason: Supports the model registry and multiple model versions; pickles match the brief's .pkl requirement.

decision: DVC tracks the whole data/ folder as one unit with tagged versions (data-v1-raw, v2-cleaned, v3-features); the local store path is kept out of Git.
reason: The history of one pointer file shows multiple data versions for the DVC screenshot.

decision: Two requirements files: requirements.txt (app only) and requirements-dev.txt (notebook and tracking).
reason: Keeps hosting installs small and fast while the notebook stays fully reproducible.

decision: Figures are saved as 'Figure <section>.<n>' in figures/ and tables as 'Table <section>.<n>' in outputs/tables/, all in the shared palette.
reason: Notebook, report and slides can cite the same numbered items.

decision: Models will be saved as dd-mm-yyyy-HH-MM-SS.pkl using config.MODEL_TIMESTAMP_FORMAT.
reason: Matches the brief and lets predictions be traced to a model.

decision: A minimal Streamlit page is deployed early as an environment check.
reason: Finds hosting and dependency problems before the final week.

decision: Read StateHoliday as text and keep codes 0, a, b, c.
reason: Avoids treating numeric 0 and text '0' as different categories.

decision: Keep every store-day (nothing deleted). Open days with zero sales are flagged (suspect_zero_sales) and excluded from training through use_for_training.
reason: Refines D06: the rows look like recording errors, but keeping them avoids creating new date gaps.

decision: Stores missing a long block of days are flagged (has_history_gap, missing_history_days); sequence and rolling features must not cross the gap.
reason: The same block is missing for every affected store and filling it would invent sales.

decision: Missing test Open values are set by the rule 'open unless Sunday or state holiday' and flagged (Open_imputed).
reason: Evidence from the same store in train supports the rule.

decision: Competition distance: median plus flag. Competitor opening dates: unknown stays unknown (flagged); years before 1990 treated as unknown.
reason: Avoids inventing competition ages; distance is a store attribute with no sales information.

decision: Promo2 details are coded as not applicable (None / 0) for stores that do not participate.
reason: The missing values are structural, not unknown.

decision: Unusual sales are flagged with a store-by-weekday robust z-score (|z| > 5) and kept; no IQR capping.
reason: A global IQR rule would remove promotion peaks and large stores; flagged rows can be tested in a sensitivity run in Section 7.

decision: Cleaned tables are saved to data/interim as train_clean, test_clean and store_clean (compressed CSV) and versioned in DVC as data-v2-cleaned.
reason: Later sections start from one agreed cleaned dataset.

decision: Final holdout = 20 Jun 2015 to 31 Jul 2015 (42 days). It is locked in code (get_masks) and every use must be written to the evaluation-access log.
reason: Gives one honest score on history never used for tuning; test.csv has no sales.

decision: Three rolling validation windows of 42 days before the holdout: rolling_1 14 Feb 2015 to 27 Mar 2015; rolling_2 28 Mar 2015 to 08 May 2015; rolling_3 09 May 2015 to 19 Jun 2015. Each window trains on all history before it (expanding window) and is forecast from one cut-off shared by all stores.
reason: Tests stability over time and matches how the real forecast will be made.

decision: Seasonal stress test: 01 Aug 2014 to 17 Sep 2014 (48 days, 935 stores with complete history). Reported alongside the rolling windows, not used for tuning.
reason: It is the only window that resembles the test window (summer school holidays about 43% vs 44%); it also covers forecast days 43 to 48.
status: Provisional (confirm in Section 7 if it disagrees with the rolling windows)

decision: Feature-availability policy enforced in code (src/validation.py): only known-future, store-static and origin-history features are allowed as inputs; Customers and cleaning controls are blocked. Engineered features must be registered with a class.
reason: Makes leakage a failed check, not a judgement call.

decision: No fitting of any kind (scalers, imputers, encoders, aggregates, models) on rows after a split's training end date.
reason: Prevents information from the forecast window entering the model.

decision: In validation windows, Open, Promo and holiday columns use their actual values, as if the plans were known in advance.
reason: The real test file supplies the same planned fields, so this mirrors how the forecast will be used.

decision: History features are computed at forecast origins (training rows built from several past origins, each looking back only from its own origin). Lag features are only allowed in a clearly labelled recursive simulation that never uses actual validation sales.
reason: Keeps training rows consistent with how forecasts are produced.

decision: The final model is refit on all labelled history only after every choice is locked.
reason: Section 10 handles the final refit and the single holdout scoring.
